answer: Orchard-Ridge Routing Depth requires each agent to route queries through a locally verified neighbor set that forms a ridge of overlapping paths; agents whose neighbors share too few second-hop connections are demoted. The signal is the orchard of distinct subgraphs an agent touches: Sybils cluster, producing shallow, redundant reach. An attacker must sustain many disjoint neighbor sets with real relay traffic, costing per-identity bandwidth and latency overhead that scales linearly with each fake node.
